cross_tool_domains.attrition: Not applicable (secondary realist review of published and grey literature with no longitudinal participant follow-up; however, full-text exclusions in PRISMA Figure 1 are embedded in an image with no bibliographic list of excluded studies).
cross_tool_domains.confounding: Not directly applicable (secondary qualitative/policy realist review without quantitative causal effect estimation; however, urban vs. rural/remote geography, state/territory fiscal capacity, and general water management vs. drinking-water-specific policy are intertwined across macro, meso, and micro CMO configurations without counterfactual separation).
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Moderate / Mixed concern: Section 2.1 explicitly defines policy as a publicly available, non-negotiable statement requiring mandatory compliance, and the review distinguishes national non-binding guidelines (ADWG) and lack of statutory enshrinement of the human right to drinking water from state/territory frameworks; however, primary statutes and enforceable regulations are not systematically cited or coded, and advisory papers, strategies, guidelines, and media articles are included alongside formal policies despite the mandatory-compliance definition.
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Moderate to high concern: Data extraction was performed by a single reviewer (Author 1) with verification by co-authors rather than independent duplicate extraction; Table 1 omits extracted aims, methods, and findings despite Section 2.9 stating they were tabulated there; Section 2.10 states the JBI Checklist for Qualitative Research was used, whereas Appendix A actually applies JBI Systematic Review and JBI Textual Evidence: Expert Opinion checklists summed with custom cultural questions into unvalidated percentage scores; and coding of contexts vs. mechanisms relied on internal team yarning consensus.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Weak / Indirect: No primary measurement or standardized quantitative extraction of drinking water quality or health outcomes was conducted; outcomes are synthesized narratively as broad policy themes (e.g., best-practice hallmarks of engagement) alongside secondary aggregate statistics cited from included reports (e.g., Wyrwoll et al. 2022 and CSIRO 2023 estimates of >400 remote/regional communities lacking safe drinking water).
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: High concern: No pre-registered realist review protocol (e.g., PROSPERO or OSF) was reported; Table 1 omits study methods, aims, and findings that Section 2.9 claims were outlined in Table 1; no list of excluded full-text studies is provided; and Appendix A quality ratings and political-bias flags on Studies 1 and 2 are omitted from the narrative Results and Discussion.
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: High concern: Although electronic searching (8 databases) and multi-reviewer screening (Authors 1-3) were systematic, micro-level policy selection relied on purposive/convenience inclusion of just 4 'best practice' local case studies (rather than systematic sampling across >500 Australian local councils) and 5 media reports, and eligibility excluded superseded policies and non-English sources without providing an excluded-studies list.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q1: Did the research questions and inclusion criteria for the review include the components of PICO?
domain_ratings.justification: Adapted for a realist policy review, Sections 2.2 and 2.7 clearly define the Population (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples in Australia), Intervention/Policy exposure (current Australian government drinking water policies linked to accountability mechanisms and Indigenous engagement), implicit multi-level Comparison (macro, meso, and micro system levels), and Outcomes (CMO configurations capturing policy design integration and drinking water equity).

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q2 [CRITICAL DOMAIN]: Did the report of the review contain an explicit statement that the review methods were established prior to the conduct of the review and did the report justify any significant deviations from the protocol?
domain_ratings.justification: Although Section 2.3 cites a general co-design protocol for the Co-design Brains Trust (Fono et al. 2024) and AIATSIS ethics approval (#REC-0161), and Section 2.10 notes a deviation from an intended CREATE quality tool, the paper contains no explicit statement that an a priori protocol specifically specifying this realist review's questions, search strategy, inclusion criteria, and synthesis methods was written or registered (e.g., PROSPERO/OSF) prior to conducting the search.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q3: Did the review authors explain their selection of the study designs for inclusion in the review?
domain_ratings.justification: Sections 2.5 and 2.7 explicitly justify including both qualitative and quantitative research methodologies alongside downloadable government policy documents, reports, and case studies in order to build a comprehensive, context-specific realist CMO synthesis across diverse evidence types.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q4 [CRITICAL DOMAIN]: Did the review authors use a comprehensive literature search strategy?
domain_ratings.justification: The authors searched 8 electronic databases (PubMed, Medline, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Academic Search Premier, AIATSIS Indigenous Studies, and Google Scholar) plus multiple grey-literature repositories and water agency websites in May 2024 (within 24 months of acceptance), reported exact Boolean search strings and MeSH terms, consulted a university librarian, and justified recency restrictions. Rated Partial Yes rather than full Yes because backward reference-list checking of included studies was not reported and English-language restriction was not explicitly justified methodologically.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q5: Did the review authors perform study selection in duplicate?
domain_ratings.justification: Section 2.8 reports that Authors 1-3 reviewed both article titles/abstracts and full texts against the eligibility criteria, with Author 2 resolving discrepancies.
domain_ratings.where_found: [PDF Page 4 of 19] (p. 605, Section 2.8 Screening and Selection)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q6: Did the review authors perform data extraction in duplicate?
domain_ratings.justification: Section 2.9 reports single-reviewer primary extraction by Author 1 followed by verification by Authors 2-6 and 9, rather than independent duplicate extraction by at least two reviewers (or >=80% agreement check on a sample) as strictly required by AMSTAR 2 Item 6.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q7 [CRITICAL DOMAIN]: Did the review authors provide a list of excluded studies and justify the exclusions?
domain_ratings.justification: Although Section 2.8 states that irrelevant articles were excluded with reasons documented and references a PRISMA flow diagram (Figure 1), no bibliographic list of potentially relevant studies excluded at full-text screening (or individual exclusion reasons) is provided in the article or appendices.
domain_ratings.where_found: [PDF Page 4, 15-19 of 19] (pp. 605, 616-620, Section 2.8 and Appendices A-B)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q8: Did the review authors describe the included studies in adequate detail?
domain_ratings.justification: Despite Section 2.9 stating that literature aim, methods, findings, and policy implications were extracted and outlined in Table 1, Table 1 only reports Evidence type, Author/year, Title, and System level (Macro, Meso, Micro), omitting study designs, populations/settings, policy interventions, and specific findings for the 38 included sources.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q9 [CRITICAL DOMAIN]: Did the review authors use a satisfactory technique for assessing the risk of bias (RoB) in individual studies that were included in the review?
domain_ratings.justification: Quality appraisal was performed on only 5 of the 38 included sources (leaving all 24 government policy reports, all 4 micro-level local case studies, and all 5 media reports completely unappraised, as acknowledged in Section 5). Furthermore, Section 2.10 mistakenly states the JBI Checklist for Qualitative Research was used, whereas Appendix A actually applies the JBI Checklist for Systematic Reviews (Studies 1 and 3) and JBI Checklist for Textual Evidence: Expert Opinion (Studies 2, 4, and 5) combined with 7 custom cultural items into unvalidated percentage grand totals.
domain_ratings.where_found: [PDF Page 4, 8, 11, 15-18 of 19] (pp. 605, 609, 612, 616-619, Sections 2.10, 5, and Appendix A)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q10: Did the review authors report on the sources of funding for the studies included in the review?
domain_ratings.justification: The authors did not report funding sources for any of the 5 peer-reviewed studies or 33 grey-literature documents included in the review.
domain_ratings.where_found: [PDF Page 5-8, 15-18 of 19] (pp. 606-609, 616-619, Table 1 and Appendix A)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q11 [CRITICAL DOMAIN]: If meta-analysis was performed did the review authors use appropriate methods for statistical combination of results?
domain_ratings.justification: No meta-analysis or quantitative pooling was performed in this realist review.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q12: If meta-analysis was performed, did the review authors assess the potential impact of RoB in individual studies on the results of the meta-analysis or other evidence synthesis?
Q13 [CRITICAL DOMAIN]: Did the review authors account for RoB in individual studies when interpreting/ discussing the results of the review?
domain_ratings.justification: In Appendix A, Studies 1, 2, and 3 received low composite ratings (~35%, ~54%, ~41%) and Studies 1 and 2 were explicitly flagged for 'questionable sources, political bias concern', yet Sections 3 and 4 cite and rely upon Studies 1-3 uncritically without discussing these quality/bias concerns. Section 5 only briefly notes that the rigour of the 4 unappraised local case studies 'may be subject to scrutiny'.
domain_ratings.where_found: [PDF Page 9-11, 15-17 of 19] (pp. 610-612, 616-618, Sections 3.4, 4, 5, and Appendix A)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q14: Did the review authors provide a satisfactory explanation for, and discussion of, any heterogeneity observed in the results of the review?
domain_ratings.justification: Consistent with realist CMO synthesis, Sections 3.4-3.7 and Section 4 systematically examine and explain contextual heterogeneity across macro (national), meso (state/territory, e.g., NSW and QLD vs. Tasmania and NT), and micro (local) governance levels, as well as disparities between urban centres and rural/remote Indigenous communities.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q15 [CRITICAL DOMAIN]: If they performed quantitative synthesis did the review authors carry out an adequate investigation of publication bias (small study bias) and discuss its likely impact on the results of the review?
domain_ratings.justification: No quantitative synthesis or meta-analysis was performed.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Q16: Did the review authors report any potential sources of conflict of interest, including any funding they received for conducting the review?
domain_ratings.justification: Funding sources (Macquarie University, University of New South Wales, Australian Government RTP Scholarship, and Onehealth Organisation) and a formal 'no conflicts of interest' declaration are reported alongside an extensive Positionality Statement disclosing authors' community, academic, and government policy roles (note that Author 8 co-authored 4 included records in Table 1, disclosed indirectly via authorship/positionality).

overall_narrative_summary: This study is a secondary realist review (synthesizing 5 peer-reviewed papers and 33 grey-literature sources—24 government documents, 4 local case studies, and 5 media articles—guided by Indigenous governance and team yarning circles with a Co-design Brains Trust) examining how Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives are integrated into Australian drinking water policy across macro, meso, and micro levels. Appraised with AMSTAR 2 as a systematic evidence synthesis, overall methodological confidence is rated Critically Low due to four critical-domain flaws (Q2, Q7, Q9, Q13) and three non-critical weaknesses (Q6, Q8, Q10). Strengths include a comprehensive 8-database and grey-literature search designed with a librarian (Q4: Partial Yes), explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (Q1, Q3: Yes), multi-author screening (Q5: Yes), strong Indigenous governance/positionality reporting (Q16: Yes), and clear realist examination of jurisdictional and urban-vs.-remote heterogeneity (Q14: Yes). However, the review reports no pre-registered review protocol (Q2: No), provides no bibliography of excluded full-text studies (Q7: No), relies on single-reviewer extraction with verification while omitting study designs and findings from Table 1 despite claiming they were tabulated there (Q6, Q8: No), purposively selects just 4 local 'best practice' case studies out of >500 councils, leaves 33 of 38 included sources completely unappraised while misstating in Section 2.10 which JBI checklists were applied in Appendix A (Q9: No), and fails to account for Appendix A's low ratings and 'political bias concern' flags when interpreting Studies 1-3 in the synthesis (Q13: No). While realist reviews follow RAMESES conventions rather than statistical meta-analysis, these reporting, selection, and appraisal-integration gaps substantially limit confidence in the completeness and evidentiary weighting of the review's conclusions.
study_design_identified: Realist review (secondary systematic review of peer-reviewed and grey literature using Context-Mechanism-Outcome [CMO] synthesis, guided by Indigenous governance and collaborative research-team yarning)
where_found_summary: Methods (Sections 2.1-2.11) on PDF Pages 2-8 (pp. 603-609); Results and Table 1 (Sections 3.1-3.9) on PDF Pages 5-10 (pp. 606-611); Discussion, Limitations, Funding, Conflicts of Interest, and Positionality Statement on PDF Pages 1, 10-12 (pp. 602, 611-613); Appendix A (Cultural and JBI quality assessments of the 5 peer-reviewed studies) on PDF Pages 15-18 (pp. 616-619). Note: Figures 1-3 are embedded graphics not rendered as plain text in the extract, whereas all text sections, Table 1, and Appendices A-B are complete.
why_tool_chosen: Although framed within realist methodology (Pawson et al. 2005) and guided by Indigenous yarning among the author team and Co-design Brains Trust, the study's empirical core is a secondary evidence synthesis with an explicit Boolean search across 8 bibliographic databases and grey-literature repositories (Section 2.6), formal inclusion/exclusion criteria (Section 2.7), multi-reviewer title/abstract and full-text screening with a PRISMA flow diagram (Section 2.8), structured data extraction (Section 2.9), and formal checklist quality appraisal of included peer-reviewed papers (Section 2.10, Appendix A). Under RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1, AMSTAR 2 is the designated appraisal tool for secondary systematic and scoping/realist reviews employing an explicit systematic search and screening method.
